method.per_member: rw_txd.read_dictionary(member_bytes) -- a refusal is recorded by its sentence with the member's name replaced by <member>; a dictionary that reads has every raster's undecodable_reason() taken, every decodable one passed through decode_rgba() and, at 8 bits, replacement_identity()

note: What mod_editor.games._formats.rw_txd makes of every RenderWare member of every mapped PlayStation 2 disc that carries one. Counts, sizes, section ids, library versions and refusal sentences only; no pixel, no palette entry and no member name from any disc is here.
question: Two Blitz discs already ship an art page on this reader. Would a third or a fourth disc read with the same code, and is Madden NFL 06 -- an EA title that carries RenderWare -- one of them?

verdicts.blitzleague_ps2: READS WITH NO CHANGE. All 4,442 .rtd members parse at library version 0x1c020020, later again, and 3,304 of 4,924 rasters decode -- 67%, the best of the four discs, because this disc's art is mostly 8-bit. The 82 .rws and 17 .dff members are refused as clumps, which is correct.
verdicts.madden06_ps2: NO TEXTURE DICTIONARY ON THE DISC. Madden NFL 06's own art is EA TERF/MMAP and SHPS; the only RenderWare is a bundled Burnout 3 demo under /BURNOUT, 178 files. All 132 RenderWare-extension members are refused, by five distinct sentences: 70 carry a section length that does not fit the member (60 .awd audio-wave dictionaries, 10 .hwd/.lwd meshes and the one .txd), 36 begin with section id 0x1d, 24 with 0x80d, 1 with 0x809 and 1 with 0x10 (a clump). The whole-member search for an embedded texture-dictionary header found one candidate in one .bgv, declaring a 13-byte body -- too small to be a dictionary and read as a coincidence. So rw_txd unlocks nothing on Madden NFL 06.
verdicts.nflblitz2002_ps2: 761 of 761 dictionaries read, 10,420 rasters, 4,189 decoded, 4,166 identities. The disc the reader was written on.
verdicts.nflblitz2003_ps2: 840 of 840 dictionaries read, 11,828 rasters, 6,392 decoded, 6,365 identities.
verdicts.nflblitzpro_ps2: READS WITH NO CHANGE. All 1,641 .rtd members parse, 17,609 rasters, and the library version is 0x1005ffff on every one -- a later RenderWare than the Blitz 2002/2003 discs' 0x0401ffff, and it made no difference to the reader. But 14,407 of the 17,609 rasters are 4-bit, so only 3,200 decode: 18% of the disc's art, against 40% and 54% on the two Blitz discs. Two 8-bit rasters are refused individually because their texel section carries no IMAGE-mode GIF tag. The 2,229 .dff members are refused as clumps, which is correct.

what_a_blitz_pro_or_madden06_art_page_wo: Blitz Pro and Blitz: The League: the reader is done and the container reader (midway_pak) is done, so an art page is the wiring -- a lane over the pack instead of over a ZIP -- plus the same 4-bit gap, which costs Blitz Pro most (only 18% of its rasters decode). Madden NFL 06: rw_txd contributes nothing; its art page is TERF/MMAP and SHPS work, which is a different reader this project already has.
what_would_make_the_madden06_negative_wr: The search looks for section id 0x16 written little-endian at a byte boundary in a member whose extension the disc map calls RenderWare. A dictionary compressed inside another container, stored big-endian, or held in a member with an extension not on that list would be missed. The disc map records no compressed container under /BURNOUT, and every EA container on the disc is TERF, which this project already reads and which holds MMAP, not RenderWare.
